newsitem.title: FRANCE: France to switch 11.1 bln Ffr in spending - Strauss.
newsitem.headline: France to switch 11.1 bln Ffr in spending - Strauss.

text.p: The French government plans a decree implementing switches in spending programmes worth 11.1 billion francs this year, Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn told a news conference.
The new spending will be financed through reallocation and scrapping of spending planned elsewhere and will not involve any net increase in 1997 spending.
"These 11.1 billion francs will be covered either through reallocations, or through scrapping of credit lines," Christian Sautter, junior minister responsible for the budget, said.
Earlier Defence Minister Alain Richard said in a radio interview that the government planned to scrap around 11 billion francs in planned spending this year.
"There is not one more franc of deficit in this decree," Strauss-Kahn said.
The new spending was split among measures aimed at boosting consumption, growth and jobs.
These include two billion francs to create 40,000 to 70,000 public sector jobs for young people.
The money would be reallocated from job creation programmes set up by the previous centre-right government which Strauss-Kahn said were not effective.
A back-to-schoool payment paid to families will be quadrupled to 1,600 francs per family at a total cost of 6.4 billion francs in 1997.

The government also plans to spend 600 million francs to help low-income people find housing, 1.15 billion francs on public housing, 290 million francs on additional school lunch subsidies, and 600 million in extra spending not accounted for in the existing budget.
